problem: Monocular (single forward RGB) VLN agents lag far behind panoramic RGB-D agents because the narrow field of view hides global layout, depth and upcoming scene cues. Prior monocular VLA methods (NaVid, Uni-NaVid, NaVILA) rely on large models and large external data, and neural-rendering approaches need extra mapping modules.
motivation: Panoramic cameras and depth sensors are costly and heavy to deploy, so monocular agents are more practical, but blind spots (side doors, stairs) hurt planning. The paper is inspired by human brain findings that people infer panoramic scenes from partial views and simulate upcoming scenes, so it asks whether the agent can internalize this imagination as latent supervision that is dropped at inference.
key_idea: Train a small VLA so its hidden state (the Unified Navigation Representation) also regresses latent features of current and next-step panoramic RGB and depth (Latent Panoramic Dreaming), giving monocular agents internalized global, geometric and future awareness at no inference cost.
insight: Ablations show that LPD is the main source of gain: on R2R-CE val-unseen (R2R-CE training data only), IR alone gives SR 37.7 and adding LPD gives SR 46.1 (SPL 32.1 to 39.9). Panoramic depth is the strongest single sub-task (SR 42.2) and all four combined are best. Predicting 1 future step is better than 2 or 3 (SR 39.1 vs 34.3 vs 29.2), and cubemap plus log-depth targets align better with pretrained encoders. The 2B model with no external data matches 8B models trained on about 2M external samples.
method: Unified Navigation Representation: the LLM backbone hidden state h_t over [instruction text, N=8 uniformly sampled history frames + current frame] is treated as a shared latent for actions and global scene features.

Latent Panoramic Dreaming: an MSE loss aligns h_t with SigLIP (weight-shared with the input encoder) latent features of the current panoramic RGB, current panoramic depth, next-step panoramic RGB and next-step panoramic depth. It is training-only; no panorama or depth is used at inference.
Supervision preprocessing: panoramas are split into a 4-view cubemap (left/front/right/back, 90° each); depth is log-scaled and colormapped to pseudo-RGB so pretrained encoders can be reused.
Action prediction: the model outputs the next K=3 actions as natural-language text (forward 25/50/75 cm, turn 15/30/45°, stop) with a cross-entropy loss.
Instruction reasoning: an auxiliary task generates the instruction from the sampled trajectory images to improve vision-language alignment.

Multi-task co-training: tasks are switched via prompts; total loss = action loss + λ·feature loss + instruction loss. NVILA-lite-2B (SigLIP + Qwen2) is fully fine-tuned on R2R-CE, RxR-CE and DAgger data.

setting.backbone: NVILA-lite-2B (SigLIP encoder + projector + Qwen2 LLM), fully fine-tuned
setting.training_data: Simulator-only: R2R-CE (320K step samples) and RxR-CE (600K) training splits, plus 500K DAgger step samples from R2R-CE environments, plus auxiliary LPD and instruction-reasoning data built on R2R-CE. No external web or VQA data.
setting.observation: monocular forward RGB with 8 sampled history frames (no depth or panorama at inference)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 25/50/75 cm, turn left/right 15/30/45°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (panoramic RGB-D used only as training-time supervision)

results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, the monocular 2B MonoDream reaches SR 55.8 / SPL 49.1 with no external data, slightly above NaVILA (SR 54.0 / SPL 49.0) and Aux-Think (SR 55.7 / SPL 48.7), both 8B models trained on about 2M external samples. On RxR-CE it gets SR 49.4, marginally above NaVILA (49.3), though SPL 40.9 trails NaVILA's 44.0; cross-dataset SR is 25.1 vs NaVid 23.8. Inference is 0.8 s/step vs 1.2 s for the 8B models.
limitations: Imagines only the current and next-step scene from monocular history, without explicit panoramic memory or reconstruction; richer temporal memory is left for future work.
Gains over the strongest monocular baselines are small (SR +0.1 on RxR-CE, +0.1 on R2R-CE vs Aux-Think), and the gap to panoramic RGB-D methods is only narrowed, not closed.
Evaluated only in simulation with no real-robot tests; longer-horizon future prediction degrades performance.
